theory.intro: A non-vertical straight-line graph shows a quantity changing at a **constant rate**: the same amount is gained or lost in every equal time interval. The gradient of the line is that rate. The line need not start at the origin. A horizontal line shows no change, so its rate is zero.
facts: For a non-vertical straight-line graph, the gradient $=\dfrac{\text{change in the quantity}}{\text{change in time}}$, and this equals the signed constant rate. A vertical line has zero change in time, so this division is undefined.
The rate can be found from **any** two points on the line — every interval gives the same rate.
The value where the line meets the vertical axis is the starting value.
steps: Read two points on the line.
Find the change in the quantity and the change in time between them.
Divide the change in the quantity by the change in time, and state the rate with its units. For a rate of decrease, state the positive amount lost per unit of time.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Read the points $(0,20)$ and $(8,60)$. The volume increases by $40$ L in $8$ minutes.
$\begin{align*}\text{Filling rate}&=\frac{60-20}{8-0}\\&=5\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
The tank starts with $20$ L. In $12$ minutes it gains $5\times12=60$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{Volume at 12 minutes}&=20+60\\&=80\text{ L}\end{align*}$

Read the points $(0,120)$ and $(6,60)$.
$\begin{align*}m&=\frac{60-120}{6-0}\\m&=-10\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
The negative gradient shows decreasing volume. The rate of decrease is $10$ L/min.
The tank must lose its starting volume of $120$ L to become empty.
$\begin{align*}\text{Time to empty}&=\frac{120}{10}\\&=12\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$

Use the endpoints of each straight section.
From $0$ to $4$ seconds, volume rises from $0$ to $40$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{First rate}&=\frac{40-0}{4-0}\\&=10\text{ L/s}\end{align*}$
From $4$ to $6$ seconds, volume stays at $40$ L. The horizontal section has a filling rate of $0$ L/s.
From $6$ to $12$ seconds, volume rises from $40$ to $60$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{Final rate}&=\frac{60-40}{12-6}\\&=\frac{10}{3}\text{ L/s}\end{align*}$
The final interval lasts $6$ seconds; it excludes the pause.

The second stage starts at $(4,60)$ and ends at $(10,30)$. The tank loses $30$ L over $6$ minutes.
$\begin{align*}\text{Rate of decrease}&=\frac{60-30}{10-4}\\&=5\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$

At $6$ minutes, hose A has delivered $15$ L and hose B has delivered $9$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{Hose A rate}&=\frac{15}{6}\\&=2.5\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Hose B rate}&=\frac{9}{6}\\&=1.5\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
Hose A fills faster. Its line is steeper on the shared axes.

Read the starting volume of $30$ L and the volume of $120$ L at $6$ minutes.
$\begin{align*}\text{Filling rate}&=\frac{120-30}{6-0}\\&=15\text{ L/min}\end{align*}$
The tank needs another $180-30=150$ L.
$\begin{align*}\text{Time to reach capacity}&=\frac{150}{15}\\&=10\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$

foundation.solution_text:
Hose A: rate $=\dfrac{9}{6}=1.5\text{ L/min}$
Hose B: rate $=\dfrac{12}{6}=2\text{ L/min}$
Hose B's line is steeper, so hose B fills faster.

Printer X: rate $=\dfrac{100-40}{10}=6\text{ percentage points/day}$
Printer Y: rate $=\dfrac{100-20}{10}=8\text{ percentage points/day}$
Printer Y's ink is dropping at the greater rate, so printer Y runs out faster.

Point $A$ is at day $2$, level $12$ cm. Point $B$ is at day $9$, level $33$ cm.
Rate $=\dfrac{33-12}{9-2}$
$=\dfrac{21}{7}$
$=3\text{ cm/day}$

development.solution_text:
The filament falls from $660$ g to $420$ g between $4$ and $20$ hours.
Rate $=\dfrac{660-420}{20-4}$
$=\dfrac{240}{16}$
$=15\text{ g/h}$

Rate $=\dfrac{45}{6}$
$=7.5\text{ L/min}$
Volume delivered in $24$ minutes $=7.5\times24$
$=180\text{ L}$

Rate $=\dfrac{200-80}{12-0}$
$=\dfrac{120}{12}$
$=10\text{ \$/week}$, so the balance grows by $\$10$ per week.

mastery.solution_text:
Rate $=\dfrac{320-200}{4}$
$=30\text{ L/min}$
$800=200+30t$
$600=30t$
$t=20\text{ minutes}$
The tank reaches capacity $20$ minutes after $t=0$; it overflows only if water continues flowing in after that.

During the pause (from $5$ to $9$ minutes) the volume stays at $100$ L, so that stage cannot be used to find the final rate.
From $9$ minutes ($100$ L) to $20$ minutes ($155$ L):
Rate $=\dfrac{155-100}{20-9}$
$=\dfrac{55}{11}$
$=5\text{ L/min}$
